concept.name: Regular trading hours
concept.definition: The principal daily trading session of a market; for U.S. exchange-listed stocks, regular trading hours run 9:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. Eastern Time. Official opening and closing prices, consolidated-volume statistics, and most regulatory protections are defined over this window.
concept.intuition: The main shift: when the market is fully staffed, liquid, and protected, and when the day's official prices are set.
concept.mechanics: During RTH all order types and protections operate (e.g., LULD price bands), the opening and closing auctions bracket the session, and quotes and trades disseminate to the consolidated tape; outside RTH, many order types and protections are unavailable.
concept.failure_modes: Assuming extended-hours behavior generalizes to RTH (or vice versa) misleads: spreads, depth, and volatility regimes differ, and strategies calibrated on RTH data can fail in thin extended sessions.
concept.misconceptions: RTH is not when 'all' trading happens — substantial volume trades in extended hours and, for futures, overnight — and the closing auction price, not the 4:00 p.m. quote alone, is the official close.
concept.example: A limit order designated DAY by a U.S. equity trader is eligible for execution only during the 9:30 a.m.-4:00 p.m. ET session unless the broker accepts extended-hours instructions.
